subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose the opt-in `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` setting and generic `onTaskTimeout` queue hook as the host contract for abandoning non-cooperative deferred context-engine maintenance?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and proven, but repository policy sets a high bar for new config and compatibility-sensitive plugin/session contracts; code review cannot decide the permanent timeout default, operator surface, and abandonment semantics.

options.title: Approve the opt-in contract
options.body: Land the current disabled-by-default setting, synchronous queue hook, and host-side fence because it fixes affected deployments without changing existing upgrades.

options.title: Use an internal host budget
options.body: Replace the public setting with an owner-chosen internal or existing compaction safety budget, then re-prove long-running plugin compatibility and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Reject abandonment semantics
options.body: Keep the linked issue open and require a cooperative context-engine cancellation or narrower plugin API contract before releasing maintenance lanes early.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Land the current disabled-by-default setting, synchronous queue hook, and host-side fence because it fixes affected deployments without changing existing upgrades.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged context-engine lifecycle history makes this person the strongest available owner for the permanent host/plugin contract.
